BREAKING • FICTIONAL

Maurice Alexander's third fine triggers automatic ban

In the original simulation's Week 10 random fine draw, Chicago wide receiver Maurice Alexander received his third cumulative fine, automatically triggering a one-game suspension for Week 11. He was one of 30 distinct fine recipients selected without performance weighting.

Meanwhile, the weighted suspension lottery selected a mix of high-profile and lower-profile players, including J.K. Dobbins (2 games), Kaleb Johnson (3), Austin Trammell (1), Breece Hall (2), Rashod Bateman (4), and Deven Thompkins (1). These are simulation outcomes, not real NFL disciplinary actions.

OFFICIAL SIMULATION RULES • HOW THE SUSPENSION LEAGUE WORKS

League methodology

The Suspension League is a fictional disciplinary overlay on real NFL fantasy football results. The actual players and their PPR scoring are real; all fines, bans, and news incidents are invented for entertainment. The league does not claim any real-world wrongdoing.

30Uniformly random fines per week
20Total bans per week
0.1Starting / reset lottery weight
3Fines per automatic ban

Step-by-step disciplinary process

01 • ELIGIBILITY

Build the player pool

Use eligible QB, RB, WR and TE players with available fantasy scoring. Anyone already serving a fictional suspension is excluded from new fine and suspension draws. In the archived 2025 model, the full pool contained 660 players.

02 • FINES

30 equal-chance draws

Select exactly 30 different eligible players uniformly at random, without replacement. Fantasy scoring, fame and position do not influence fines. Each player's chance of being fined that week is 30 ÷ number eligible (4.545% in a 660-player opening pool).

03 • FINE HISTORY

Fines accumulate

Every fine increases the player's future suspension-lottery weight by 1 percentage-point unit. Fine history persists even after serving a ban. Every third cumulative fine (3, 6, 9…) automatically triggers a one-game suspension.

04 • WEEKLY SCORING

Performance changes risk

For eligible players, add 10% of that week's nonnegative actual PPR points to their lottery weight. All players begin at 0.1 weight units; prior unsuspended accumulated weight carries forward. Weights are relative chances in a draw, not literal percentages or guaranteed outcomes.

05 • SUSPENSION LOTTERY

Fill 20 total bans

First count automatic third-fine bans. Fill the remaining slots through weighted selection without replacement among eligible players who were not fined that same week. The total is exactly 20 newly issued bans per week.

06 • RESET & RETURN

Serve the sentence

When suspended, a player's lottery weight resets to 0.1, but cumulative fines remain. A ban issued after Week W applies from Week W+1 through Week W+length. Players return when that period ends.

Suspension length lottery

For suspensions selected by the regular lottery, duration is determined using this weighted distribution. Automatic third-fine suspensions are always one game.

Ban lengthProbability
1 game50%

Fantasy scoring and roster consequences

A suspended player scores zero simulated fantasy points while serving the ban, even if they play in the real NFL. The real-world PPR scoring remains available for reference. The live 2026 version uses ESPN league #25556 as its primary scoring source and will identify fantasy-team owners only when verifiable.

How the first live 2026 report starts

The live launch is a clean-slate inaugural draw: every player begins with zero fines, no active fictional suspension, and 0.1 initial weight. NFL Week 10, 2026 is designated Simulation Week 1. Subsequent simulation weeks preserve the ledger, accumulated fines and active bans; they do not restart from zero. A first-week third-fine ban is impossible.

About this archive demonstration

This sample website shows Week 10 of the previously run 2025 historical simulation, where prior fines and suspensions had already accumulated. That is why it demonstrates a third-fine automatic ban. It is separate from the fresh-start 2026 live season. Source workbook: 2025_Fantasy_Discipline_Uniform_Fines_Rerun.xlsx (seed 20251121).

Fairness and transparency

Uniform fines are never performance-weighted. Suspension selection is performance-weighted, but every eligible player can be drawn. Exact individual suspension probabilities depend on the weights of all other candidates and the sequence of draws; a displayed weight alone is not a probability.

ALL ARTICLES AND DISCIPLINARY INCIDENTS ARE FICTIONAL FANTASY SIMULATION EVENTS. NO REAL MISCONDUCT IS ALLEGED.
